edits_applied.before: Lin Xiangru came back from the meeting at Mianchi and was made shangqing, the highest ministerial rank, placed above Lian Po. Lian Po was Zhao's finest general: he had beaten Qi, taken Yangjin and won a name for courage among the states. His reaction was blunt. Lin Xiangru had earned his place with nothing but his tongue; why should he sit above me? He announced that the next time they met he would humiliate the man. What makes the episode hard is that the grievance had grounds. Lian Po really had great merit from storming cities and fighting in the field, while Lin Xiangru's credit was entered under words. Now both held the top rank at court: one meant to humiliate, the other hid.

edits_applied.before: 到了秦廷，秦王在章台接见相如，接过璧大喜，传给身边的美人和侍从看，左右都高呼万岁。相如看出秦王无意偿城，上前说璧有小毛病要指给秦王看，拿到璧便「持其璧睨柱，欲以撃柱」。秦王怕他砸碎，连忙道歉，召来管图籍的官员，指着地图说从这里过去的十五座城给赵。相如判断这不过是做样子，城根本拿不到，于是说和氏璧是天下共传之宝，赵王送来前斋戒五日，秦王也该斋戒五日，设九宾于廷，他才敢献璧。秦王答应了，把他安置在广成传舍。相如断定秦王即便斋戒也一定违约，就让随从穿上粗布衣，把璧揣在怀里，从小路逃走，送回赵国。等再次上廷，他把话摊开：秦自缪公以来二十多位国君，没有一位说话算数；璧已送回赵国，「臣知欺大王之罪當誅，臣請就湯鑊」。秦王与群臣相视而嘻，左右有人要把他拉下去，秦王最终说，杀了相如也得不到璧，反而断了秦赵之好，不如以礼相待送他回去，「卒廷見相如，畢禮而歸之」。

edits_applied.before: At the Qin court the king received Lin Xiangru in the Zhang Terrace, was delighted with the jade, and passed it around to his ladies and attendants, who all cried long life to him. Lin Xiangru saw he had no intention of paying. He said the gem had a small flaw he would point out, took it back, and stood holding it with his eyes on a pillar, ready to smash it. The alarmed king apologised, sent for the official in charge of maps and pointed out fifteen cities for Zhao. Lin Xiangru judged this mere show. The Heshi jade was a treasure the whole world talked of, he said; the king of Zhao had fasted five days before sending it, and the king of Qin should fast five days and hold the nine-fold ceremony at court before he would dare present it. The king agreed and lodged him at the Guangcheng hostel. Sure that the king would break his word even after fasting, Lin Xiangru had a follower put on coarse clothes, hide the jade in his robe and take it home to Zhao by back roads. At the next audience he laid it out: in more than twenty reigns since Duke Mu, Qin had never kept a firm agreement; the jade was already back in Zhao; "I know that deceiving Your Majesty is a crime deserving death, and I ask to go to the cauldron." The king and his ministers looked at one another. Some attendants moved to drag him out, but the king reasoned that killing him would not bring back the jade and would end good relations with Zhao. In the end he received Lin Xiangru at court with full ceremony and sent him home.

edits_applied.before: Before the meeting at Mianchi the king of Zhao, afraid of Qin, did not want to go. Lian Po and Lin Xiangru took counsel and told him that staying away would show Zhao weak and afraid. So the king went, and Lin Xiangru with him. The king agreed. At Mianchi the king of Qin, to the end of the banquet, could not gain the upper hand over Zhao; Zhao, for its part, had massed its forces to meet Qin, and Qin dared not move.

edits_applied.before: In King Huiwen's time Zhao acquired the Heshi jade from Chu, and King Zhaoxiang of Qin wrote offering fifteen cities for it. The king of Zhao consulted his great general Lian Po and the other ministers, and both answers looked bad: hand it over and the cities might never come, leaving Zhao cheated; refuse, and Qin's armies might. Nothing was settled, and there was no one fit to carry the reply to Qin. Miao Xian put forward Lin Xiangru, and told a story against himself. He had once been guilty of an offence and meant to flee to Yan. Lin Xiangru stopped him: Zhao was strong and Yan weak, and the king of Yan had courted Miao Xian only because he stood in the king of Zhao's favour; flee there, and Yan would tie him up and send him back. Better to "strip and lie on the block", as the phrase went, and ask pardon. Miao Xian did, and the king pardoned him.

edits_applied.before: At the Qin court the king received Lin Xiangru in the Zhang Terrace, was delighted with the jade, and passed it around to his ladies and attendants, who all cried long life to him. Lin Xiangru saw he had no intention of paying. He said the gem had a small flaw he would point out, took it back and stood against a pillar, his hair bristling with anger, and denounced the king, warning that he would dash his own head and the jade together against the pillar. Only then did he stand holding the jade with his eyes on the pillar, ready to bring it down. The alarmed king apologised, sent for the official in charge of maps and pointed out fifteen cities for Zhao. Lin Xiangru judged this mere show. The Heshi jade was a treasure the whole world talked of, he said; the king of Zhao had fasted five days before sending it, and the king of Qin should fast five days and hold the nine-fold ceremony at court before he would dare present it. The king agreed and lodged him at the Guangcheng hostel. Sure that the king would break his word even after fasting, Lin Xiangru had a follower put on coarse clothes, hide the jade in his robe and take it home to Zhao by back roads. At the next audience he laid it out: in more than twenty reigns since Duke Mu, Qin had never kept a firm agreement; the jade was already back in Zhao; "I know that deceiving Your Majesty is a crime deserving death, and I ask to go to the cauldron." The king and his ministers looked at one another. Some attendants moved to drag him out, but the king reasoned that killing him would not bring back the jade and would end good relations with Zhao. In the end he received Lin Xiangru at court with full ceremony and sent him home.
